inputs.root_cause: SAL-XLIFF-OBL-D2BB0F0D8018D601 (XLIFF-PARSE-001) named the xliff root's spec-mandated xml:space default value as untested and unmodeled -- the reader never synthesized a default when the attribute was absent from the source XML.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 4 new tests prove a new XliffDocument.xml_space property returns 'default' when the attribute is absent (the spec-mandated root default), the explicit value when present, and that the raw attributes dict still separately distinguishes absent from an explicitly-written 'default' for any caller needing that finer distinction.
inputs.regression_tier: full xliff package suite (tests/python/xliff) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Read the obligation's own rule_text precisely before scoping the fix: '(XLIFF core - whitespace and language) The xliff root declares xml:space with default value default, and source and target permit optional xml:lang and xml:space attributes' -- confirmed this is narrower than the full XML spec's per-element xml:space inheritance rule.

2. Read the pinned XLIFF 2.1 spec source directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xliff-001.bin, section 4.3.2.2) for xml:space's own value-description and default-value entry: 'Value description: default or preserve... Default value: ...When used in <data>: The value preserve. When used in <xliff>: The value default. When used in any other element: The value of the xml:space attribute of its parent element.' Confirmed the obligation's own rule_text deliberately scopes to only the root's default (xliff -> 'default'), not the full file/group/unit/source/target/data inheritance chain -- correctly not attempting the broader chain as a separate, larger feature.

3. Added a new xml_space property to XliffDocument, returning attributes.get(XML_SPACE_KEY, 'default') -- exposing the spec-mandated root default explicitly, mirroring the same 'expose an existing default explicitly' pattern used elsewhere this session (e.g. ORA's version-drift warning, NRRD's version_requirements).

4. Verified interactively before writing formal tests: absent xml:space correctly reports 'default'; explicit 'preserve' and explicit 'default' both report verbatim; the raw attributes dict still distinguishes absent from explicit-default at the finer level XLIFF-PRESERVE-001 already cares about -- all 3 cases correct on the first attempt.

5. Wrote 4 formal tests covering all cases plus the absent-vs-explicit-default distinguishability check. Ran ruff (clean), the full xliff suite (381 passed, was 377, +4), and the full 6-format regression (3136 passed, was 3132, +4; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

6. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-27584d624a7398e7, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.
